question.text: A curved in a level road has a radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>75</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The maximum speed of a car turning this curved road can be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> without skidding. If radius of curved road is changed to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>48</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and the coefficient of friction between the tyres and the road remains same, then maximum allowed speed would be _____  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

solution.text:
The maximum speed is given as v=μgr, where, μ is coefficient of friction and r is radius of curved road.

⇒v1v2=r1r2

⇒30v2=7548=2516=54

⇒v2=24 m s-1
